plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in forms ranging from pompons to spidery and decorative types. It thrives in cool autumn weather and is a staple of late-season gardens and floral markets in the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan); widely grown in North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants, so they start forming flower buds only when nights lengthen. Growers manipulate light to make them bloom out of season, and the flower is the emblem of Japan's Imperial family.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like foliage that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. The blossoms carpet streets and gardens as they fall, creating purple-tinted ground cover.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Brisbane, Sydney, Grafton), and New Zealand's north
plants.funFact: Pretoria, South Africa, is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, which turn the city purple every spring. Many Australian university students traditionally associate the blooms with approaching exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that is one of the earliest camellias to flower, producing fragrant single or semi-double blooms with prominent golden stamens against glossy dark green leaves. It tolerates more sun than other camellias and is popular as hedging.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and their seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, used in Japan for cooking, hair care, and polishing tools.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up leafless stems topped with umbels of narrow, wavy-petaled, sparkling pink flowers in late autumn, when most other garden plants have faded. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (October to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; naturalized or cultivated in the UK, Western Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: The petals of Nerine have a glittering, crystalline sheen that sparkles in sunlight, earning it the nickname 'diamond lily'. The bulbs bloom best when crowded and baked by summer sun.
